question: A mother asks why her toddler needs a mix of both animal and plant proteins. What's the best way to answer?

options.A: Mixing them ensures the child gets all the essential building blocks for growth
options.B: Animal proteins contain no essential amino acids on their own
options.C: Plant proteins are toxic to the kidneys of young children
options.D: Only animal proteins can provide energy for daily physical activities

explanation: Spot on. Combining different protein sources helps make sure the child gets every essential amino acid their growing body needs!

question: Which specific medication is used to treat encephalitis caused by the herpes simplex virus?

options.A: Acyclovir
options.B: Ibuprofen
options.C: Penicillin
options.D: Fluconazole

explanation: Acyclovir is our go-to antiviral medication for herpes virus infections, including nasty cases of viral encephalitis. You'll see this drug very often in clinical practice!

question: What is the primary cause of inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Long-term exposure to environmental toxins
options.B: Severe bacterial infections in early childhood
options.C: Faulty genes passed down from parents
options.D: Nutritional deficiencies during pregnancy

explanation: These conditions stem from genetic mutations inherited through family bloodlines rather than external lifestyle factors. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h1)

question: What is an important step before putting a fresh layer of ointment on a patient's skin?

options.A: Apply a drying alcohol swab over the entire lesion
options.B: Scrub the area vigorously with an antiseptic brush
options.C: Warm the skin using a high-heat therapeutic lamp
options.D: Gently cleanse the skin to remove old medication

explanation: Always wash away old residue gently! This prevents buildup, stops irritation, and lets the fresh medicine do its job properly.

question: A patient feels she has lost her independence after starting to use a wheelchair, even though her family says she can still do a lot. What kind of loss is this?

options.A: Physical loss
options.B: Perceived loss
options.C: Actual loss
options.D: Situational loss

explanation: You got it! A perceived loss is uniquely felt inside by the person, and others might not always see or measure it the same way.

question: In nursing and science, what does 'pH' stand for?

options.A: Power of hydration
options.B: Pressure of homeostasis
options.C: Potential of hydrogen
options.D: Percentage of hydroxyl

explanation: pH simply stands for the 'potential of hydrogen'. It tells us how many free hydrogen ions are floating around in a fluid, which determines how acidic or basic it is!

question: Why should a nurse be concerned if a patient breaks a bone easily from just a minor bump or fall?

options.A: It raises suspicion for underlying bone weakness or metabolic bone disease
options.B: It confirms the patient has normal bone mineral density
options.C: It indicates that the patient has a severe muscular infection
options.D: It proves the patient engages in professional contact sports

explanation: Spot-on! Bones shouldn't break from minor bumps. This is a huge warning sign for conditions like osteoporosis.

question: What makes a clinic truly "youth-friendly" when it comes to reproductive health?

options.A: Programs that focus solely on treating severe physical trauma injuries
options.B: Medical facilities that treat only patients under twelve years of age
options.C: Clinics that operate exclusively during late night hours on weekends
options.D: Services that offer confidential, non-judgmental care tailored to teenagers

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics win teens' trust by keeping their business private, listening without scolding, and treating them with absolute respect.

question: How do peer support groups help teenagers living with a chronic condition like HIV?

options.A: They eliminate the side effects of antiretroviral medications.
options.B: They replace the need for professional nursing assessments entirely.
options.C: They reduce feelings of isolation and encourage treatment adherence.
options.D: They provide financial loans for higher education expenses.

explanation: Well done! Connecting with others facing the same journey helps teens share tips, stay on their meds, and realize they aren't alone.

question: Why is proper cleaning and drying of nebulizer equipment so critical for patient safety?

options.A: Dirty equipment will permanently break the air compressor motor
options.B: Washing prevents the plastic mask from changing color over time
options.C: Moist plastic parts easily grow harmful bacteria that can cause lung infections
options.D: Leftover medication residue turns into a solid metal inside the tube

explanation: Wet nebulizer cups are breeding grounds for germs, which the patient would inhale directly into their lungs during the next treatment. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)

question: What happens when families treat reproductive health as a strictly taboo subject?

options.A: The adolescent brain accelerates its prefrontal cortex development
options.B: Young people develop stronger coping mechanisms for peer pressure
options.C: Adolescents seek out answers from peers and media, which can be inaccurate
options.D: Teenagers naturally decide to practice strict abstinence until marriage

explanation: Silence at home drives curious teenagers to search elsewhere for information, often gathering dangerous myths and misinformation. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h5)

question: How do the four scales of measurement relate to one another?

options.A: Lower scales are more accurate than higher ratio scales
options.B: Nominal and ratio scales are identical except for their names
options.C: All four scales share the exact same mathematical properties
options.D: Higher scales build upon the rules of lower scales by adding features

explanation: Each scale keeps the perks of the previous one while adding a cool new mathematical power. Nominal is basic, ordinal adds rank, interval adds equal spacing, and ratio adds true zero!

question: A healthy adult client closes their eyes and relaxes quietly. Which brain wave pattern is most likely to become dominant?

options.A: Beta waves
options.B: Theta waves
options.C: Delta waves
options.D: Alpha waves

explanation: When you close your eyes and just chill out, your brain shifts into alpha wave mode. You've got this!

question: Why does severe anaemia put a mother at high risk for heavy bleeding after delivery (postpartum hemorrhage)?

options.A: The placenta remains permanently attached to the uterine wall
options.B: The exhausted uterine muscle fails to contract effectively after delivery
options.C: Low red blood cells cause high blood pressure in the arteries
options.D: Blood clotting factors are completely absent in all pregnant women

explanation: Think of it this way: muscles need oxygen to work hard. When blood is low on oxygen-carrying red cells, the uterus gets tired and can't clamp down tightly after birth to shut off the bleeding vessels.

question: Why are fast transport and clear communication so vital during a maternity emergency referral?

options.A: It allows the receiving hospital to prepare a private room
options.B: It prevents dangerous delays in treating life-threatening complications
options.C: It reduces the administrative paperwork for the nursing staff
options.D: It ensures the maternity home gets a refund for medical supplies

explanation: Spot on! Every minute counts in an emergency, and cutting down delays saves lives.

question: How do clinical audits and case reviews help improve healthcare delivery in a PAC unit?

options.A: By identifying system weaknesses and learning from them to prevent future errors
options.B: By creating strict rules that punish nurses for asking questions
options.C: By increasing the waiting time for patients arriving at the emergency room
options.D: By replacing all doctors and nurses with automated computer software

explanation: Good case reviews focus on fixing teamwork and hospital systems rather than pointing fingers, creating a much safer environment for both patients and staff.

question: What are the classic warning signs of peritonitis in a patient getting IP therapy?

options.A: A high fever accompanied by a persistent dry cough
options.B: Sudden swelling and redness of the lower legs
options.C: Cloudy effluent drainage and severe abdominal pain
options.D: Complete inability to speak or swallow food

explanation: Spot on! If the drained fluid looks cloudy instead of clear, paired with bad belly pain, it's a huge red flag for peritonitis (infection). [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h6)

question: What do we call the swelling that happens when fluid gets trapped in body tissues?

options.A: Atrophy
options.B: Sclerosis
options.C: Oedema
options.D: Necrosis

explanation: Spot on! Oedema is just the clinical word for when excess fluid builds up in the spaces between your body tissues, causing that puffy look.

question: A patient on chemo for bone sarcoma has a temperature of 38.5°C and chills. What is your priority nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to put on a heavy sweater and drink hot tea
options.B: Administer a dose of routine oral pain medication for the chills
options.C: Notify the healthcare provider immediately for potential neutropenic sepsis
options.D: Document the finding in the chart and recheck the temperature in six hours

explanation: Chemo lowers white blood cells, making fever a true medical emergency. Always report it right away to protect your patient from sepsis!

question: Why do we need to eat water-soluble vitamins more often than fat-soluble ones?

options.A: They cannot be absorbed without large amounts of dietary fat.
options.B: They are destroyed instantly by stomach acid during digestion.
options.C: The liver stores them in massive quantities that deplete rapidly.
options.D: Excess amounts are quickly flushed out of the body in the urine.

explanation: Exactly! Because they dissolve in water, your kidneys easily wash away any daily extra. That's why a steady daily supply from your diet is key.

question: A patient remembers their childhood clearly but cannot recall what they ate an hour ago. What kind of memory loss is this?

options.A: Global retrograde amnesia wiping out all past decades
options.B: Anterograde amnesia with preserved remote memory
options.C: Pure procedural amnesia affecting motor skills only
options.D: Transient global amnesia that will resolve in hours

explanation: You've got it! 'Anterograde' means trouble making *new* memories, while older childhood memories ('remote memory') stay safe in the back of the mind.

question: Why is a kidney infection (pyelonephritis) so dangerous for a pregnant woman?

options.A: It thickens the amniotic fluid until fetal movement stops completely
options.B: It stops the liver from producing essential blood-clotting proteins
options.C: It can trigger systemic sepsis and stimulate premature uterine contractions
options.D: It automatically causes permanent blindness in the developing fetus

explanation: High fever and severe infection put the whole body under massive stress, which can easily trick the womb into starting early labor.

question: What classic physical change is often seen with long-term steroid therapy (cushingoid features)?

options.A: Yellowing skin
options.B: Excessive hair loss
options.C: Enlarged hands
options.D: Moon face

explanation: A round, puffy face—often called a 'moon face'—is a classic sign that the body has been exposed to extra corticosteroids over time.

question: Why do we need a whole team of different specialists (a multidisciplinary team) in neuro-rehab?

options.A: Hospital regulations require at least five different specialists to sign off on every therapy session.
options.B: It ensures that the client spends the entire day participating in continuous physical exercise.
options.C: Neurological deficits affect many different aspects of physical, cognitive, and social function.
options.D: Physicians are generally unable to manage any physical therapy exercises on their own.

explanation: Brain and nerve issues don't just affect walking—they can touch speech, thinking, emotions, and movement. That's why working together as a team gives the patient the best possible support!

question: Why is forced marriage considered a violation of human rights?

options.A: It strips away personal autonomy and freedom of choice
options.B: It prevents families from sharing their wealth
options.C: It always involves cross-border international travel
options.D: It violates traditional wedding ceremony laws

explanation: Forcing someone into a marriage removes their basic human right to choose their own life partner and future. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which of these skin conditions needs careful medical evaluation rather than just reassurance?

options.A: Mild palmar erythema on the hands
options.B: Linea nigra across the lower abdomen
options.C: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
options.D: Spider angiomas on the upper chest

explanation: While lines and spider veins are harmless, cholestasis involves the liver and requires close monitoring to keep the baby safe.

question: How do nursing theorists define 'health' within our professional framework?

options.A: A dynamic state of physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The complete elimination of all hospital admissions nationwide
options.C: The total absence of any identifiable bacteria in the blood
options.D: A static condition achieved strictly through pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health isn't just the literal absence of sickness. In nursing, we see it as a flowing, everyday state of overall physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: What pocket of pus can develop near the fallopian tube and ovary during a bad pelvic infection?

options.A: Cervical retention nodule
options.B: Endometrial polyp
options.C: Uterine fibroid cyst
options.D: Tubo-ovarian abscess

explanation: When upper reproductive infections get severe, pus can collect and form a painful pocket involving both the tube and the ovary, called a tubo-ovarian abscess.

question: What tool do healthcare workers mainly use to check if children and teens (ages 2 to 20) are underweight or carrying excess weight?

options.A: Waist-to-hip ratio formulas
options.B: Total daily calorie calculations
options.C: BMI-for-age percentile charts
options.D: Standard adult body mass index tables

explanation: Correct! Because kids and teens are still growing, we use special age- and sex-matched charts instead of standard adult tables to see how they're doing.

question: What must legally happen before a nurse can begin last offices?

options.A: Arrival of the mortuary attendants at the ward
options.B: Formal certification of death by a physician
options.C: Payment of all hospital bills by the family
options.D: Completion of the police report for the incident

explanation: A doctor must officially confirm and document death before any last offices or body transfers can take place. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: How can you tell the difference between morning joint stiffness in osteoarthritis versus inflammatory arthritis?

options.A: Osteoarthritis stiffness only affects the upper body joints.
options.B: Osteoarthritis stiffness never happens in the morning hours.
options.C: Osteoarthritis stiffness usually lasts less than thirty minutes.
options.D: Osteoarthritis stiffness gets worse the more the person moves.

explanation: Joint stiffness from wear-and-tear arthritis is brief after waking up, whereas inflammatory arthritis causes stiffness lasting an hour or more. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: A patient recovering from a hip replacement cannot bend past 90 degrees. Which tool helps them put on shoes safely?

options.A: A four-wheeled walker
options.B: A standard metal cane
options.C: A set of axillary crutches
options.D: A long-handled shoehorn

explanation: Brilliant! A long-handled shoehorn lets them reach their feet easily without breaking their hip movement rules.

question: What is the main goal of periodic evaluation during rehabilitation?

options.A: To permanently discharge the patient from follow-up
options.B: To see if goals are met and adjust interventions if needed
options.C: To punish the patient for slow physical recovery
options.D: To increase the cost of hospital equipment rentals

explanation: Spot on! Regular check-ins let the care team see what is working and tweak the plan if the patient hits a roadblock.

question: Why must you stay right by the patient during the first 15 minutes of a blood transfusion?

options.A: Hospital accreditation rules require physical presence to document vital signs
options.B: Most severe, life-threatening transfusion reactions occur during this initial window
options.C: Patients often feel lonely and anxious when receiving intravenous fluids
options.D: Pumps automatically lock out nurse access after fifteen minutes of running

explanation: Most bad reactions happen right at the beginning when the blood first hits circulation. Staying close lets you catch it instantly!

question: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), how is health best defined today?

options.A: Having adequate financial resources to access medication
options.B: The total absence of diagnosed chronic or acute illnesses
options.C: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.D: Living in a rural area with low population density

explanation: You've got this! Modern health isn't just about not being sick in bed—it looks at your whole life: physical, mental, and social wellness combined.

question: What is a main goal of counseling a patient *before* they take an STI test?

options.A: Administering therapeutic antibiotics before laboratory confirmation returns
options.B: Explaining test procedures and infection window periods to the client
options.C: Providing the client with their final laboratory test results immediately
options.D: Forcing the client to disclose the names of all past sexual partners

explanation: Pre-test counseling helps prep the patient so they know what to expect and understand why timing (the window period) is everything.

question: A patient waiting for a fasting blood sugar test looks pale, shaky, and dizzy. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask the lab tech to draw their blood right now
options.B: Give them a cup of hot black coffee with sugar
options.C: Check their blood sugar level immediately for low blood sugar
options.D: Tell them to keep waiting patiently for their turn

explanation: Safety first! Shaking, dizziness, and paleness during a fast are classic signs of hypoglycemia. Assess their blood sugar right away before doing anything else.

question: What is the main type of tissue found in the hypodermis (the layer right under the skin)?

options.A: Adipose tissue
options.B: Dense regular connective tissue
options.C: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.D: Nervous tissue

explanation: Correct! The hypodermis is mostly made of adipose (fat) tissue, which keeps us warm, stores energy, and cushions our organs.

question: What problem is a varicocele repair surgery designed to fix in men?

options.A: Infection in the prostate gland
options.B: A hormonal imbalance in the pituitary gland
options.C: Enlarged veins in the scrotum that warm the testes
options.D: A complete lack of sperm production in the bone marrow

explanation: Varicoceles trap heat in the scrotum, which hurts sperm. Repairing them cools things down and helps sperm grow healthy again!

question: What is the specific function of the auditory association area?

options.A: To register the raw pitch and volume of a loud noise
options.B: To interpret the meaning of sounds and spoken words
options.C: To control the physical movement of the tiny ear bones
options.D: To maintain balance and posture during head rotation

explanation: While the primary cortex hears the noise, the association area figures out what the noise actually means, such as recognizing speech. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h4)

question: A client comes to you asking for advice on diet and irregular ovulation. What is the best starting point?

options.A: Focus on whole foods, healthy weight management, and essential micronutrients
options.B: Rely entirely on heavy vitamin supplements instead of eating meals
options.C: Drink large amounts of caffeinated coffee to boost resting metabolism
options.D: Eliminate all carbohydrates completely from your daily meals

explanation: Awesome choice! Real, wholesome food and steady weight management give the body the stable foundation it needs for natural hormonal balance.

question: What major change happens to the liver tissue during cirrhosis?

options.A: Overgrowth of active healthy hepatocytes
options.B: Replacement of normal tissue with permanent scar tissue
options.C: Enlargement of bile storage ducts
options.D: Complete disappearance of the hepatic artery

explanation: Think of cirrhosis as chronic injury that causes the soft working tissue of the liver to turn into hard scar tissue (fibrosis).

question: Which of these is a key nursing action when assessing someone with a degenerative disease?

options.A: Prescribing new gene-therapy medications
options.B: Reversing the genetic mutation in the laboratory
options.C: Performing major orthopedic surgery
options.D: Evaluating motor strength and skin integrity

explanation: Spot on! As nurses, we keep a close watch on muscle strength, movement, and skin health to keep our patients as safe and comfortable as possible.

question: A stable patient complains that monthly clinic visits for pill refills make them miss work and spend too much on transport. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Require the patient to come to the clinic twice a week instead
options.B: Scold the patient for not prioritizing clinic visits over their job
options.C: Enroll the patient in a multi-month dispensing program if they are stable
options.D: Tell the patient they can stop taking their medication entirely

explanation: Brilliant! Multi-month dispensing gives stable patients several months of drugs at once, saving them transport money and protecting their daily work life.

question: Why should a nurse inspect product packaging expiration dates before gathering IV supplies?

options.A: Hospital management penalizes nurses who waste old stock
options.B: Plastic catheters become too hard to puncture skin over time
options.C: Expired items may have lost their sterile barrier
options.D: Saline flushes expire and turn acidic inside plastic

explanation: Sterile packaging guarantees infection prevention; if the date has passed, sterility is no longer assured. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h3)

question: When is an exchange transfusion chosen over standard phototherapy?

options.A: When bilirubin levels are critically high and threatening the brain
options.B: When the baby develops a mild diaper rash during light treatment
options.C: When the baby has mild jaundice lasting longer than two weeks
options.D: When the mother wants to formula feed instead of breastfeeding

explanation: An exchange transfusion is an emergency procedure used when bilirubin levels are dangerously high, quickly swapping the baby's blood to protect their brain.

question: A patient with psychomotor seizures has a history of a severe car accident two years ago. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Traumatic brain injury scarring
options.B: Degenerative autoimmune decline
options.C: Congenital metabolic defect
options.D: Primary brain tumor growth

explanation: Head injuries can disrupt brain pathways and leave scar tissue behind, which acts like a tiny spark plug for seizures later on. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h2)

question: You just received a delivery of delicate protein medications for your ward. What is your very first priority?

options.A: Place the vials in a warm blanket warmer to activate them
options.B: Store them openly on the nurse's station desk for easy access
options.C: Crush the vials to prepare liquid doses for oral feeding tubes
options.D: Check and follow the required cold-chain refrigeration rules

explanation: Biotech protein drugs are super fragile! They'll lose their potency quickly if they aren't kept at the right cold temperature right away.

question: Which of these patients has the highest risk of developing an obstetric fistula?

options.A: A young rural mother who laboured at home for three days without skilled help
options.B: A middle-aged woman being treated for an uncomplicated bladder infection
options.C: A pregnant woman who attends all her routine antenatal care appointments
options.D: An older woman scheduled for an elective Caesarean section at a tertiary hospital

explanation: Spot on! Days of unmanaged labour without emergency care is the classic pathway to tissue damage and fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h2)

question: Why is it so important for young neurons to migrate to new locations in the developing brain?

options.A: It prevents neurons from dividing too quickly inside the spinal canal
options.B: It directly creates the protective myelin covering around nerve fibers
options.C: It seals the neural tube to prevent fluid leakage
options.D: It ensures that neurons reach their correct final locations to form functional layers

explanation: You got it! Neurons must travel from where they are born to their precise final spots so the brain can build its proper layered structure.

question: What is the main goal of providing top-notch reproductive health services in a community?

options.A: Higher rates of untreated sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Decreased maternal and neonatal complications
options.C: Increased maternal and neonatal mortality
options.D: Reduced healthcare utilization among young adults

explanation: You got this! Good reproductive health services catch things early and educate mothers, keeping both them and their babies safe from harm. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the main medical goal right before a scheduled thyroid surgery for an overactive thyroid?

options.A: Inducing temporary hypothyroidism to prevent weight gain
options.B: Clearing all stored iodine from the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Completely eliminating the body's need for future hormone pills
options.D: Achieving a normal, stable metabolic hormone level

explanation: Spot on! Operating on someone with wild, unmanaged hyperthyroidism can trigger a dangerous hormone surge, so stability is a must first.

question: Why does diabetes mellitus significantly increase a person's risk for developing CAD?

options.A: Pancreatic failure lowers the overall volume of body fluids
options.B: High blood sugar damages blood vessel linings over time
options.C: Extra sugar in the blood thickens the heart valves directly
options.D: Diabetes forces the kidneys to stop producing red blood cells

explanation: Chronic high blood glucose levels injure the delicate inner lining of arteries, making it much easier for plaque to form. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does the term 'fidelity' mean when talking about healthcare simulators?

options.A: How easily the simulator can be moved between classrooms
options.B: How closely the simulation mimics a real-life clinical situation
options.C: How much the simulator costs to purchase and maintain
options.D: How many students can use the simulator at the same time

explanation: Fidelity describes the level of realism and how well the simulation copies actual patient care scenarios. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why do nurses view substance abuse as a chronic brain condition rather than a lack of willpower?

options.A: It only affects people who have inherited genetic immune deficiencies
options.B: It permanently alters neural pathways and changes how the brain functions
options.C: It prevents the liver from producing enough blood cells for survival
options.D: It is classified as a physical injury caused by accidental trauma

explanation: Exactly! Repeated drug use actually rewires brain chemistry and structure. Seeing it as a medical condition helps us care for patients with real empathy.

question: When giving total care to a very ill patient, what is your absolute top priority?

options.A: Maintaining airway patency and breathing efficiency
options.B: Providing a full bath every morning
options.C: Encouraging heavy oral fluid intake
options.D: Ensuring clean bed linens and fresh hospital gowns

explanation: Oxygen is king! Keeping the airway clear is always priority number one because without oxygen, nothing else matters.

question: When does a pregnant woman's blood pressure usually drop to its lowest point?

options.A: During the second trimester
options.B: Right before active labour begins
options.C: During the first few weeks postpartum
options.D: Immediately after delivery

explanation: You got it! Vascular resistance drops around mid-pregnancy, bringing blood pressure down before it goes back up near term.

question: Which fasting plasma glucose level is considered diagnostic for diabetes mellitus?

options.A: 100 to 125 mg/dL
options.B: 70 to 99 mg/dL
options.C: Below 60 mg/dL
options.D: 126 mg/dL or higher

explanation: A fasting blood sugar reading of 126 mg/dL or higher measured on two separate occasions is one of the standard diagnostic cutoffs for diabetes. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the most crucial piece of advice for a patient sent home with a 14-day course of antibiotics for salpingitis?

options.A: Save half the pills in case the infection returns next month
options.B: Double the dose if you miss a pill during the middle of the week
options.C: Stop taking the medication as soon as your pelvic pain goes away
options.D: Finish every single pill, even if you start feeling completely better

explanation: Feeling better doesn't mean all germs are gone. Stopping early can let tougher bacteria survive and bring the infection right back.

question: A client with rheumatoid arthritis on long-term steroids lifts a light bag and suddenly feels sharp back pain. What complication should you suspect?

options.A: A vertebral compression fracture due to bone weakening
options.B: An acute flare of ankylosing spondylitis in the lower spine
options.C: A minor muscle strain that will resolve with resting in bed
options.D: A systemic infection spreading rapidly through the bloodstream

explanation: Long-term steroid use weakens bones (causing osteoporosis), making clients very vulnerable to sudden spinal compression fractures from even minor movements like lifting.

question: How do metabolic joint diseases mainly differ from normal wear-and-tear osteoarthritis?

options.A: Metabolic disorders stem from chemical and biochemical faults rather than simple wear and tear
options.B: Osteoarthritis affects only the upper limbs while metabolic diseases target the spine
options.C: Osteoarthritis is caused by uric acid accumulation exclusively
options.D: Metabolic joint diseases cannot be managed with medications

explanation: Spot on! While regular osteoarthritis comes from physical joint usage over time, metabolic diseases are all about how the body handles its internal chemistry.

question: What does a radical prostatectomy involve?

options.A: Radiation treatment applied only to the renal pelvis
options.B: Surgical removal of the entire prostate gland
options.C: Chemical blockage of male hormones in the testes
options.D: Destruction of bladder stones using laser energy

explanation: When a patient has localized prostate cancer, a radical prostatectomy is done to take out the whole prostate gland and some nearby tissues to get the cancer out.

question: How does a 'stimulation test' help us figure out an endocrine issue?

options.A: It forces the pancreas to stop making insulin during high stress
options.B: It tests if an underactive gland can produce hormones when given a trigger
options.C: It measures the permanent destruction of the pituitary stalk
options.D: It permanently blocks all hormone receptors in peripheral tissues

explanation: You're doing great! If a gland is acting lazy, we give it a special trigger (stimulation) to see if it still has the energy to wake up and produce hormones.

question: Why does cellular damage occur during prolonged shock?

options.A: Blood vessels expand and physically crush nearby organs
options.B: Cells lack oxygen to produce energy and waste builds up
options.C: Excess water floods the cells and causes them to burst
options.D: White blood cells mistakenly attack healthy body tissue

explanation: Without a steady supply of oxygen, cells cannot make normal energy, causing harmful waste products to accumulate and damage cellular structures. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h1)
